chat.author: Brian Campbell
chat.text: "Other use cases that need more power and coverage." Do they really? What are they? And does any of it really warrant another way of doing this?

chat.author: Brian Campbell
chat.text: there's already more than one...

chat.author: Christian Bormann
chat.text: fair point!

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: @Aaron didn't you have a CIMD driver for this as well? Would oyu like to highlight it?

chat.author: Yaroslav Rosomakho
chat.text: @Brian, I believe this would be strictly better compared to the sad common practice of a static client_secret

chat.author: Brian Campbell
chat.text: agree to disagree i think

chat.author: Brian Campbell
chat.text: justin!

chat.author: Christian Bormann
chat.text: you have a bit of echo justin

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: thanks, must have fallen over something during the reconnect

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: wow 15/15 people responded, impressive

chat.author: Dick Hardt
chat.text: I'd suggest keeping this focused on the specific OAuth use case and not the generic client authentication use case.

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: This isn't meant to be a generic client authenticaiton mechanism outside of oauth, so we agree there

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: Keeping the scope narrow would be super important

chat.author: Dick Hardt
chat.text: Aaron seems to think that it is gneric building on how CIMD works.

chat.text: CIMD is oauth specific

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: CIMD is also an OAuth thing
